desc:
A museum is open from time 0 to time T. Each visitor group stays for a half-open range [start, end) with 0 ≤ start < end ≤ T. The groups are in no particular order.

Return an array res of length n + 1 (where n is the number of groups) such that res[c] is the total length of time, inside [0, T), during which exactly c groups are in the museum. The entries always add up to T.

intervals = [[1, 3], [2, 4]], T = 5  ->  [2, 2, 1]

Nobody is inside during [0, 1) and [4, 5) (2 units), exactly one group during [1, 2) and [3, 4) (2 units), and two groups during [2, 3) (1 unit).
constraints: intervals[i] = [start, end] with 0 ≤ start < end ≤ T
hints: T can be 10<sup>9</sup>, so you cannot loop over every time unit. How many different times can the crowd size change at?
Between two consecutive event times (starts and ends of the groups) the crowd size is constant. Sort the distinct event times.

Keep the current crowd size c and the previous event time. At each new event time t add t - prev to res[c], then apply the change (+1 for starts, -1 for ends) of all events at t. Finally add T - prev to res[0].
editorial: Collect the net change of the crowd size for every distinct event time in a map. Process the times in increasing order, remembering the previous time and the crowd size that held since then. The stretch [prev, t) had exactly c groups, so add its length to res[c]; then update c with the net change at t.

Before the first event and after the last one the museum is empty, so the stretch from 0 to the first event time and the stretch from the last event time to T both go to res[0] (the code handles the first one with prev = 0 and c = 0). Using net changes per time removes any worry about the order of starts and ends at the same time. O(n log n) time because of the sort, O(n) space.
solution:
def timeAtEachLevel(intervals, T):
    delta = {}
    for s, e in intervals:
        delta[s] = delta.get(s, 0) + 1
        delta[e] = delta.get(e, 0) - 1
    res = [0] * (len(intervals) + 1)
    crowd = 0
    prev = 0
    for t in sorted(delta):
        res[crowd] += t - prev
        crowd += delta[t]
        prev = t
    res[crowd] += T - prev
    return res
